override.reason: Extracting drive() into helpers would separate each engine call from the tally increment that must sit ON the issuing line - that adjacency IS the independence property under test, and breaking it is exactly the M5 defect the rework was reopened to fix. expectations() is long because it must name ten fields and, per criterion C3, carry each field's independent source beside its value; splitting it would recreate the source-drifts-from-value failure the Expect class exists to prevent. Length here is a consequence of a documented correctness requirement, not of poor decomposition.

smells.finding: _ControlRun has 11 methods/attributes with one clear responsibility (drive one checklist through the real engine CLI and tally what it issued). Expect and _Refused are two- and zero-field value objects. No god class.

OBSERVATION, not a blocker. Three near-identical blocks read the step manifest as bytes and json-decode it: _ControlRun.expectations (lines 536-539), _ControlRun.manifest (613-614), and test_a3_a_null_manifest_does_not_read_as_success (908-909). The A3 test additionally re-implements the fixture's repo bootstrap (git init + two config calls) already present in the control fixture (633-635). A shared _read_manifest_bytes(path) and a _temp_git_repo(path) helper would remove both. I deliberately do NOT push harder: the third copy sits inside expectations(), and any helper it called would become a new identifier in the AST scan of layer (b), so the deduplication interacts with the independence guard and is not a free move. Worth a follow-up only if F1's layer-(b) fix lands first.

compare_fields and compare_manifest_rows are free functions over two plain dicts/lists and belong where they are - they are deliberately NOT methods on _ControlRun, because a comparison owned by the thing being compared is the self-comparison defect this file exists to detect. expectations() reads self's own tallies. No method is more interested in another object's data than its own.

The recurring {root, path, rev} triple is already a named row shape produced by expected_rows and consumed by compare_manifest_rows, and it mirrors the manifest's on-disk schema rather than inventing one. The (value, source) pair is already extracted into the Expect class - the textbook remedy, applied.

Field names are bare strings throughout (MECHANICAL_GROUP, FORBIDDEN_IDENTIFIERS, AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS, ALLOWED_FLAGS are all frozensets/tuples of str), and mismatches are returned as list[str]. An enum or a FieldName newtype is the usual remedy.

override.repo_standard: The file's own documented design rule, stated in the module docstring and in compare_fields's docstring: 'The comparison returns a list of mismatched field NAMES, never a boolean... that is what lets the red-proofs assert mismatches == ["failed-commands"]'; and the wider inherited rule that a check must name what failed rather than report a bare non-zero exit.
override.reason: The strings are not stand-ins for a missing type - they ARE the wire-level field names of the mechanical bin defined in docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 4, and they cross a process boundary into JSON where they must be strings anyway. Wrapping them would add a translation layer between the assertion text and the artifact it describes, weakening exactly the property (assertion names the field) the epic is enforcing. REFUSED, the one place a sentinel genuinely was needed, IS a dedicated class rather than a magic string, which shows the judgment was applied rather than skipped.

OBSERVATION, and it is the structural root of my finding F2. A single conceptual change - 'this control may now issue string X' - requires edits in up to four disjoint places: ALLOWED_FLAGS, AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS, the text_bearing set-equality literal in test_control_records_nothing_agent_authored, and the docstring sentence stating the count. Commit 283175b had to touch all four to add --claimed-by, and the fact that --cond, --evidence, --type and --from were never added to AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS is the same scatter biting a second time. Not a blocker: the closed-world ALLOWED_FLAGS arm is the primary defence and it is genuinely closed, so a missed AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS entry degrades reporting rather than detection.

The file changes for one reason: the mechanical bin's capture guarantee. The C5/C6 cross-run-retrieval half (from line 979) is a second concern in the same file, but it is scoped by an explicit banner comment and shares the acceptance surface capability:cross-run-retrieval named in the same gate's anchors, so it is one gate's evidence, not two axes of change.

self.path.parent / 'context' / f'{step}.json' is pathlib composition, not a train wreck through foreign objects. _git(...).stdout.strip() is one hop off a CompletedProcess. No a.b().c().d() chain reaching through several owners.

Every apparent generality is exercised: both branches of the role/refusals REFUSED split are driven (parent claimed, child unclaimed); _flag_pairs's value-starts-with-dash-dash branch is reachable and I proved it fires (N5); expected_rows's absent-file branch is reached by test_a3. The one genuinely unexercised path is the multi-element artifact-ref list, which is the opposite problem - under-exercised existing behaviour, filed as F3 - not machinery built for a hypothetical future.

THIS IS THE HEADLINE SMELL OF THE DIFF AND IT IS A REAL DEFECT, not a style note. The file's comment-to-code ratio is extreme and, in two places, the prose asserts guarantees the code does not deliver - which is the precise failure mode this epic's doctrine names ('assert against the behaviour, never against text that describes it'). (1) test_every_field_has_a_named_independent_source's docstring states layer (b) exists because '(a) is defeated by exactly one thing: a name bound at import time (from episode_capture import reopen_total), which no attribute patch can reach' - I measured that adding ' as _rt_alias' to that exact import defeats layer (b) too, suite green at 15 passed (F1). (2) test_control_records_nothing_agent_authored's docstring states 'the control hands the engine exactly TWO agent-supplied strings' - I measured a hand-typed sentence reaching the 'run' mechanical field with the census green (F2), and --cond is a third uncounted string inside the census's own scope. In both cases the comment is doing work the assertion does not, which is the definition of deodorant. Explicitly NOT flagged: the many comments that cite an issue number and explain a non-obvious mechanism (#360 on manifest path derivation, #315 on the command branch discarding stdout, #357 on the child never receiving a lease). Those record findings that cost real time to obtain and are the good kind. The remedy is to correct two sentences, not to strip the commentary.
